title: [epic] Social login at the provider: an OAuth 2.1 AS of mimid's own, with Google and GitHub federated behind it
description:
Mark 2026-11-24: "login with Google" means two different things in mimid, and
the answer differs by boundary. This epic is the provider half. The agent half
is a decision that is already made (decision bead under mimid-1wgh) plus two
children of mimid-e13m.

THE TWO BOUNDARIES.

| Boundary | What an account is there | Does OIDC fit |
|---|---|---|
| Provider (mimid-server), user <-> their provider | A real account: a MIMI URI, a bearer token (`mimid admin ... token`), storage, a web-facing HTTPS service | Yes. Here. |
| Agent front ends (JMAP, IRC), user <-> their own local daemon | No account at all: the agent serves one user and holds their MLS keys | No. |

THE CRUX, AND THE PART PEOPLE GET WRONG. The client never talks to Google. The
provider runs its OWN OAuth 2.1 authorization server, and Google and GitHub are
upstream IdPs behind it. mimid issues its own tokens. Why, and not
direct-to-Google tokens:

- AUDIENCE BINDING. A Google access token is for Google's APIs. What is needed
  is a token whose audience is mimid's JMAP endpoint (RFC 8707 resource
  indicators, RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata).
- GITHUB IS NOT AN OIDC PROVIDER. Plain OAuth 2.0, no id_token. A GitHub
  identity cannot be verified the way a Google one is; the API has to be called
  as the user. Only an AS of mimid's own can normalise that.
- LIFETIME, SCOPES AND REVOCATION stay mimid's. Revoking a device must be a
  mimid operation, not a trip to someone's consent screen.
- A STABLE LOCAL SUBJECT. The MIMI URI must outlive the IdP link: a user who
  unlinks Google keeps their identity and their rooms.

THE PIECES, FOR JMAP. RFC 8620 puts authentication out of scope and points at
bearer tokens; the ecosystem convention (Fastmail, Stalwart) is OAuth bearer
tokens discovered from the 401 on /.well-known/jmap. On top of that: RFC 8414 AS
metadata and RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, so a client finds the AS from
the resource; PKCE (RFC 7636) mandatory, authorization code only, no implicit;
RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, since every JMAP client that might show up
cannot be pre-registered; RFC 8628 device authorization grant for anything that
cannot host a redirect; refresh tokens with rotation and per-device revocation,
which maps onto the credential table's one-row-per-device model.

ONE MIMID-SPECIFIC CAUTION. The agent holds MLS keys and plaintext. An
IdP-authenticated session may mint a credential; it must never be able to
extract key material. That boundary does not move. And linking Google must not
make Google an authority over an MLS identity: credential type (BasicCredential
today, did:webvh, X.509) is a separate question from how a user logs in.

NOT IN THE DESIGN DOCS TODAY beyond frontend-auth.md's two "not offered" lines
(§4.1 OAUTHBEARER, §4.2 No OAuth), which are about the agent and stay right.
This epic needs its own design note before code.
notes:
CORRECTION (2026-11-24), after Mark asked whether this means running an
Authentik. It does not, and this epic as first written overstated the
commitment. There are THREE sizes of "login with Google", and only the
third needs an authorization server at all.

1. TODAY: nothing. The provider issues bearer tokens with `mimid admin ...
   token`, one per device, revocable, and the agent uses them. Nothing in
   this epic changes or replaces that.

2. SOCIAL LOGIN THAT MINTS A CREDENTIAL (bead mimid-e13m.15) needs mimid to
   be an OIDC RELYING PARTY only: a login page doing an authorization-code
   flow with PKCE against Google, verifying the id_token, requiring
   email_verified, and minting an app password. A client, not a server. No
   AS, no dynamic client registration, no device grant, no refresh-token
   rotation. A `[oidc]` table naming the client id, and a few hundred
   lines. THIS IS THE CHEAP PATH AND IT DELIVERS WHAT USERS ASK FOR.

3. AN AUTHORIZATION SERVER OF MIMID'S OWN is needed only for third-party
   JMAP clients to obtain tokens by OAuth, which is what the rest of this
   epic's children describe. There the real choice, not stated before, is
   BUILD IN or DELEGATE:

   - BUILD IN: mimid-server grows the endpoints over its existing token
     table. Nothing extra to operate.
   - DELEGATE to Authentik, Keycloak, Ory Hydra, Zitadel or Dex: mimid
     becomes a resource server only (validate the token, publish RFC 9728
     metadata naming the AS). Much less code, but another service to run,
     secure and back up.

   For a personal provider, delegating trades little code for a lot of
   operations, so building the narrow version in looks better. Mark decides;
   bead mimid-hb5z.1's design note answers it before any code.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE CHILDREN. mimid-hb5z.2, .3, .6, .7 and .8 are all
size 3 and wait on that choice. mimid-hb5z.4 (the upstream IdPs) and .5
(linking on the subject, never the email) are needed by size 2 as well, and
.5 is the one that is a security bug if skipped at any size.
